notes.claim: Specific heat capacity is how much energy it takes to warm 1 kg by 1 degree, and water's is 4,200 J per kg per degree Celsius.
Seawater has a density of about 1025 kg/m³ and a specific heat of about 3850 J/(kg °C); the numbers used for gravity here are g about 9.8 m/s².

sources.title: Specific heat capacity - Temperature changes and energy - Edexcel - GCSE Physics (Single Science) Revision - Edexcel - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: The specific heat capacity of water is 4,200 joules per kilogram per degree Celsius (J/kg°C). This means that it takes 4,200 J to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1°C.

sources.title: Properties of seawater
sources.quote: If the pressure change is 100 decibars (100 dbar), gravity g = 9.8 m/sec^2, and density is 1025 kg/m^3, then the depth change is 99.55 meter.

sources.title: Properties of seawater
sources.quote: The density of seawater is about 1025 kg/m^3 and the specific heat is about 3850 J/(kg C).
